prompt: R parser #line directive placement constraint vs C
answer:
In R, `#line` must begin at the very start of the line: `#` must be the first five characters, so whitespace before it is not allowed.

In C, a preprocessing directive may have whitespace before `#` (and whitespace may separate `#` from `line`). Thus, R’s placement constraint is stricter than C’s. R also treats any text following the `#line` directive on that line as a comment, whereas in C the directive continues to the newline and extra non-whitespace text may cause an error or change its meaning.
